conbody.p: Reviewing commits helps you understand how the work on a branch changes the project itself. This helps you build a mental model of how the work done on multiple branches affects the project. This mental model is useful when performing merge-like operations between branches and helps prevent merge conflicts.

Review commits on Git History or in an external application of your choice. The following sections describe how to review an individual commit, compare multiple commits, and compare the working copy with a previous revision.
The Git History table lists commits in order from latest to oldest.

section.title: Review a commit
section.p: To review a commit, select it in the Git History table and the Commit details and Affected resources panes update with the following information:

row.entry: Commit hash, commit parent hash, author, date, and committer.

section.title: Compare multiple commits
section.p: Select multiple revisions to see what changed between the latest and oldest selected commit.
To compare multiple revisions, add them to a revision comparison. To add commits to a revision comparison, go to Git History.

Use the following controls to add and remove revisions from the comparison:
Hold Control and select to add an individual commit or remove a selected commit.
Hold Shift and select to add multiple commits at once or remove multiple selected commits.
Select any commit to end the revision comparison.
The bottom-left Commit details pane updates with the start and end point of the comparison.
The bottom-right Affected resources pane lists the files modified after the oldest commit.

section.title: Compare working copy with prior revisions
section.p: Compare your working copy with another revision to view the differences between the working copy and that revision.

p.note: To access this feature, your working copy must have uncommitted changes.

section.p:
To compare your working copy with a revision, follow these steps:
Define the start and end points of the comparison.
To do so, follow these steps in any order:
Select the gray Uncommitted changes node, which represents the current working copy.
Select a revision to compare against your working copy. Select either first. Hold Shift or Control + select to select the second choice.
View which files changed on Affected Resources.
